justifications.functional_suitability: Patient & Scheduling Service (SchedulingEngine clash checks), EMR Service with Audit Logger, and Billing & Claims Service (Claims Processor) cover R-01 to R-04. Gaps: no explicit registration/demographic component, no insurance claim submission to payers/clearinghouse, no admissions element.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Redis cache (CacheManager, Clinical Cache Component), PgBouncer pooling, Kafka asynchronous events and gRPC internal calls target the EMR P95 <1 s. Gaps: no horizontal scaling or autoscaling, no load targets, and the cache invalidation strategy is unspecified.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability Service with Data Transformer (camel-fhir), FHIR Outbound Connector (mTLS), Schema Registry and Kafka decouple HL7 FHIR exchange with Lab & Imaging Systems. Gaps: outbound push only, no inbound FHIR API or lab results ingestion, and no FHIR server.
justifications.usability: Patient BFF and Staff BFF give persona-specific interfaces, and Notification Service sends reminders. Gaps: no web or mobile UI containers are modeled, there is no accessibility or localization mechanism, and Patients and Medical Staff have only generic HTTPS interfaces.
justifications.reliability: Patroni & etcd failover, Redis Sentinel, Kafka KRaft quorum, Circuit Breaker, Dead Letter Channel, transactional outbox and Barman backups are concrete. Gaps: no active-active multi-region deployment, API Gateway/service redundancy is unspecified, and the single PostgreSQL primary conflicts with the 99.99% active-active target.
justifications.security: External IdP provides MFA via OIDC/SAML, Auth Enforcement Filter validates tokens, and pgcrypto/pgaudit provide AES-256 at rest. mTLS, Redis ACL Manager, the Audit & Compliance Interceptor, AuditLogger (signed immutable logs) and tokenized Payment Integration support HIPAA/GDPR accountability.
justifications.maintainability: Services are separated by domain (Patient & Scheduling, EMR, Billing, Interoperability) with BFFs, an event bus and layered components (controller, repository, audit aspects). Gaps: shared PostgreSQL couples services, and polyglot stacks (Java, .NET, Python) add overhead.
justifications.portability: Open-source, container-friendly technologies (PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, Kong) and S3-compatible tiered storage suit hybrid deployment. Gaps: no deployment model for on-prem-k8s versus eu-central-1, no infrastructure-as-code, and no explicit cloud abstraction or Kubernetes elements.

sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio for EMR reads
Redis is wired only to Patient & Scheduling in L2
tradeoffs: Caching speeds loads but risks stale clinical data
PERF-01.justification: Cache component, PgBouncer and Redis HA support sub-second loads. But no EMR-to-Redis relationship at L2, no invalidation strategy and no load evidence. Plausible, with unaddressed risks.

tradeoffs: Async decoupling protects EMR but delays visibility
Shared PostgreSQL couples ingestion and EMR reads
PERF-02.justification: Interoperability only pushes outbound to lab systems; no inbound FHIR ingestion into EMR is modelled. Kafka decoupling and a dead-letter channel help, but the ingest path must be added.

sensitivity_points: No cross-site active-active or global traffic routing
tradeoffs: Synchronous replication prevents data loss but adds latency
AVAIL-01.justification: Patroni and Sentinel give local HA, but no deployment view shows active-active across on-prem and eu-central-1. There is no global load balancing, cross-site replication or failover design to meet zero data loss and 1-minute restoration.

tradeoffs: Retries ensure completion but risk duplicate claims
Synchronous replication reduces data loss but raises write latency
AVAIL-02.justification: Patroni gives automated DB failover and ACID transactions. But Billing has no outbox, idempotency or retry mechanism, so duplicate or lost claims are unaddressed. Needs significant additions.

sensitivity_points: Clearinghouse formatting sits inside Claims Processor
No clearinghouse adapter or port abstraction
tradeoffs: Single billing service is simple but couples integrations
Kafka decoupling isolates EMR but not claim logic
MOD-01.justification: Billing is separate from EMR, so EMR stays unchanged. But clearinghouse formatting is embedded in Claims Processor with no adapter interface, so changes may touch multiple billing components.

sensitivity_points: No UI container or component modelled
tradeoffs: Aspect-based audit reduces change but may miss new fields
Shared database eases consistency but couples services
MOD-02.justification: Controller, repository, audit logger and BFF would change, likely exceeding three components. No UI component is modelled and no schema-evolution mechanism exists. Audit via AOP helps somewhat, but the change is doubtful within one sprint.

sensitivity_points: Failed logins may not reach audit
tradeoffs: External IdP reduces effort but adds dependency
Gateway enforcement is central but a single point of failure
SEC-01.justification: External IdP with MFA and token validation at the gateway block access without a second factor. However, nothing monitors failed attempts or raises alerts within 1 minute, so recording and alerting are unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: EMR audit not stated as tamper-evident
tradeoffs: AOP audit gives coverage but adds read latency
Long retention raises storage cost and GDPR erasure conflict
SEC-02.justification: Audit logging via AOP, pgaudit, gateway interceptor and Barman retention are present. But no policy check for unrelated patient access, and only Patient service logs are signed. Authorization and tamper-evidence in EMR are missing.
